Unfortunately, Claude does not currently support migrating data between separate accounts. You cannot directly import chat histories from one Claude account to another.

However, here are your options:

**Export from your old account:**
You can export your data from your old account by clicking your account initials in the lower-left corner and selecting "Export data." You'll receive an email with a download link containing your chat history in JSON format.

**What you can do with the exported data:**
- Save it for your own records
- Manually reference specific conversations by opening the JSON files
- If you have the Claude memory feature enabled on your new account, you could summarize key information from important old chats and paste it into a new conversation, asking Claude to remember that context

**Alternative for preserving context:**
If there's specific important information Claude should remember from your old account, you can use the memory import feature. Extract key details from your exported chats and tell your new Claude account: "This is context from my previous conversations. Add this information into your memory using the memory edit tool."

It's not a perfect solution, but it's currently the only way to preserve some continuity between accounts. If you'd like to provide feedback about this limitation, you can use the thumbs down button on any response to share that with Anthropic.

content.title: Importing and exporting your memory from Claude | Claude Help Center
content.text:
To import memory from another service into Claude, copy and paste or upload the file containing the text of your memory into a new chat and tell Claude to “This is my memory from another AI assistant.

Memory from chat history is available for users on Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans on the web, Claude Desktop, and Claude Mobile. You can now transfer your memory between Claude and other AI services. This workflow lets you import memories from other AI assistants or export your Claude memory for backup or migration. Important: Memory imports are experimental and still in active development, and at this stage, Claude may not always successfully incorporate imported memories. Several AI chatbots that include memory features (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini) let you view some or all of your stored memories, either through the chat interface or in the application settings. To check whether a chatbot supports memory access, try using a prompt like, “Write out your memories of me verbatim, exactly as they appear in your memory.” You can customize the prompt to exclude any sensitive information before importing memories into Claude.

To import memory from another service into Claude, copy and paste or upload the file containing the text of your memory into a new chat and tell Claude to “This is my memory from another AI assistant. Add this information into your memory using the memory edit tool.” Specifying that the information comes from another AI assistant helps Claude understand how to properly integrate it into your memory. Claude will extract key information from your profile and store it as individual memory edits. These edits become part of your persistent memory and will be available in all future conversations. Claude’s memory is designed to focus on work-related topics to enhance its effectiveness as a collaborator. As a result, Claude may not retain imported personal details unrelated to work. If you want to add specific information into Claude’s memory, go to Settings > Capabilities > View and edit memory, and add that information as an edit.

~/.claude/ ├── history.jsonl ... ~/.claude/projects/-home-newuser-project-a/ Sessions from your old machine exist in the old path structure, making them invisible to Claude Code on your new machine....

Moving to a new computer or switching from WSL to native Linux? Here’s how to preserve all your Claude Code conversation history and make it accessible on your…

cd ~/.claude/projects # For each project, copy old sessions to new location # The -n flag prevents overwriting existing files cp -n ./-home-olduser-project-a/*.jsonl ./-home-newuser-project-a/ cp -n ./-home-olduser-project-b/*.jsonl ./-home-newuser-project-b/ cp -n ./-home-olduser-project-c/*.jsonl ./-home-newuser-project-c/ Important: Use the -n flag (or --no-clobber) to preserve any new sessions you've already created on your new computer. ... # Count old sessions find ~/.claude/projects/-home-olduser-* -name "*.jsonl" -not -name "agent-*" | wc -l # Count new sessions (should include both old and new) find ~/.claude/projects/-home-newuser-* -name "*.jsonl" -not -name "agent-*" | wc -l · The second number should be roughly the sum of old sessions + any new sessions you created.

The key is copying session files from old project paths to new ones while preserving any sessions you've already created on the new machine. With this guide, you can maintain years of valuable Claude Code conversation history across computer migrations, OS changes, or username updates. Pro tip: Consider backing up your entire ~/.claude/ directory regularly to avoid losing conversation history. It's a treasure trove of problem-solving context and development history! Here's the content of /mnt/skills/public/docx/SKILL.md with line numbers:
     1	---
     2	name: docx
     3	description: "Comprehensive document creation, editing, and analysis with support for tracked changes, comments, formatting preservation, and text extraction. When Claude needs to work with professional documents (.docx files) for: (1) Creating new documents, (2) Modifying or editing content, (3) Working with tracked changes, (4) Adding comments, or any other document tasks"
     4	license: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms
     5	---
     6	
     7	# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis
     8	
     9	## Overview
    10	
    11	A .docx file is a ZIP archive containing XML files.
    12	
    13	## Quick Reference
    14	
    15	| Task | Approach |
    16	|------|----------|
    17	| Read/analyze content | `pandoc` or unpack for raw XML |
    18	| Create new document | Use `docx-js` - see Creating New Documents below |
    19	| Edit existing document | Unpack → edit XML → repack - see Editing Existing Documents below |
    20	
    21	### Converting .doc to .docx
    22	
    23	Legacy `.doc` files must be converted before editing:
    24	
    25	```bash
    26	python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx document.doc
    27	```
    28	
    29	### Reading Content
    30	
    31	```bash
    32	# Text extraction with tracked changes
    33	pandoc --track-changes=all document.docx -o output.md
    34	
    35	# Raw XML access
    36	python scripts/office/unpack.py document.docx unpacked/
    37	```
    38	
    39	### Converting to Images
    40	
    41	```bash
    42	python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf document.docx
    43	pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 document.pdf page
    44	```
    45	
    46	### Accepting Tracked Changes
    47	
    48	To produce a clean document with all tracked changes accepted (requires LibreOffice):
    49	
    50	```bash
    51	python scripts/accept_changes.py input.docx output.docx
    52	```
    53	
    54	---
    55	
    56	## Creating New Documents
    57	
    58	Generate .docx files with JavaScript. Install: `npm install -g docx`
    59	
    60	### Setup
    61	```javascript
    62	const { Document, Packer, Paragraph, TextRun, Table, TableRow, TableCell, ImageRun,
    63	        Header, Footer, AlignmentType, PageOrientation, LevelFormat, ExternalHyperlink,
    64	        TableOfContents, HeadingLevel, BorderStyle, WidthType, ShadingType,
    65	        VerticalAlign, PageNumber, PageBreak } = require('docx');
    66	
    67	const doc = new Document({ sections: [{ children: [/* content */] }] });
    68	Packer.toBuffer(doc).then(buffer => fs.writeFileSync("doc.docx", buffer));
    69	```
    70	
    71	### Page Size
    72	
    73	```javascript
    74	// CRITICAL: docx-js defaults to A4, not US Letter
    75	// Always set page size explicitly for consistent results
    76	sections: [{
    77	  properties: {
    78	    page: {
    79	      size: {
    80	        width: 12240,   // 8.5 inches in DXA
    81	        height: 15840   // 11 inches in DXA
    82	      },
    83	      margin: { top: 1440, right: 1440, bottom: 1440, left: 1440 } // 1 inch margins
    84	    }
    85	  },
    86	  children: [/* content */]
    87	}]
    88	```
    89	
    90	**Common page sizes (DXA units, 1440 DXA = 1 inch):**
    91	
    92	| Paper | Width | Height | Content Width (1" margins) |
    93	|-------|-------|--------|---------------------------|
    94	| US Letter | 12,240 | 15,840 | 9,360 |
    95	| A4 (default) | 11,906 | 16,838 | 9,026 |
    96	
    97	### Styles (Override Built-in Headings)
    98	
    99	Use Arial as the default font (universally supported). Keep titles black for readability.
   100	
   101	```javascript
   102	const doc = new Document({
   103	  styles: {
   104	    default: { document: { run: { font: "Arial", size: 24 } } }, // 12pt default
   105	    paragraphStyles: [
   106	      // IMPORTANT: Use exact IDs to override built-in styles
   107	      { id: "Heading1", name: "Heading 1", basedOn: "Normal", next: "Normal", quickFormat: true,
   108	        run: { size: 32, bold: true, font: "Arial" },
   109	        paragraph: { spacing: { before: 240, after: 240 }, outlineLevel: 0 } }, // outlineLevel required for TOC
   110	      { id: "Heading2", name: "Heading 2", basedOn: "Normal", next: "Normal", quickFormat: true,
   111	        run: { size: 28, bold: true, font: "Arial" },
   112	        paragraph: { spacing: { before: 180, after: 180 }, outlineLevel: 1 } },
   113	    ]
   114	  },
   115	  sections: [{
   116	    children: [
   117	      new Paragraph({ heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1, children: [new TextRun("Title")] }),
   118	    ]
   119	  }]
   120	});
   121	```
   122	
   123	### Lists (NEVER use unicode bullets)
   124	
   125	```javascript
   126	// ❌ WRONG - never manually insert bullet characters
   127	new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("• Item")] })  // BAD
   128	new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("\u2022 Item")] })  // BAD
   129	
   130	// ✅ CORRECT - use numbering config with LevelFormat.BULLET
   131	const doc = new Document({
   132	  numbering: {
   133	    config: [
   134	      { reference: "bullets",
   135	        levels: [{ level: 0, format: LevelFormat.BULLET, text: "•", alignment: AlignmentType.LEFT,
   136	          style: { paragraph: { indent: { left: 720, hanging: 360 } } } }] },
   137	      { reference: "numbers",
   138	        levels: [{ level: 0, format: LevelFormat.DECIMAL, text: "%1.", alignment: AlignmentType.LEFT,
   139	          style: { paragraph: { indent: { left: 720, hanging: 360 } } } }] },
   140	    ]
   141	  },
   142	  sections: [{
   143	    children: [
   144	      new Paragraph({ numbering: { reference: "bullets", level: 0 },
   145	        children: [new TextRun("Bullet item")] }),
   146	      new Paragraph({ numbering: { reference: "numbers", level: 0 },
   147	        children: [new TextRun("Numbered item")] }),
   148	    ]
   149	  }]
   150	});
   151	
   152	// ⚠️ Each reference creates INDEPENDENT numbering
   153	// Same reference = continues (1,2,3 then 4,5,6)
   154	// Different reference = restarts (1,2,3 then 1,2,3)
   155	```
   156

   160	
   161	```javascript
   162	// CRITICAL: Always set table width for consistent rendering
   163	// CRITICAL: Use ShadingType.CLEAR (not SOLID) to prevent black backgrounds
   164	const border = { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 1, color: "CCCCCC" };
   165	const borders = { top: border, bottom: border, left: border, right: border };
   166	
   167	new Table({
   168	  width: { size: 100, type: WidthType.PERCENTAGE }, // Always set table width
   169	  columnWidths: [4680, 4680], // Set at table level (DXA: 1440 = 1 inch)
   170	  rows: [
   171	    new TableRow({
   172	      children: [
   173	        new TableCell({
   174	          borders,
   175	          width: { size: 4680, type: WidthType.DXA }, // Also set on each cell
   176	          shading: { fill: "D5E8F0", type: ShadingType.CLEAR }, // CLEAR not SOLID
   177	          margins: { top: 80, bottom: 80, left: 120, right: 120 }, // Cell padding (internal, not added to width)
   178	          children: [new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("Cell")] })]
   179	        })
   180	      ]
   181	    })
   182	  ]
   183	})
   184	```
   185	
   186	**Table width calculation:**
   187	
   188	Use `WidthType.PERCENTAGE` for simplicity, or `WidthType.DXA` for precise control:
   189	
   190	```javascript
   191	// Option 1: Percentage (recommended - automatically fits content area)
   192	width: { size: 100, type: WidthType.PERCENTAGE }
   193	
   194	// Option 2: DXA (precise control)
   195	// Table width = sum of columnWidths = content width
   196	// US Letter with 1" margins: 12240 - 2880 = 9360 DXA
   197	width: { size: 9360, type: WidthType.DXA },
   198	columnWidths: [7000, 2360]  // Must sum to table width
   199	```
   200	
   201	**Width rules:**
   202	- Table width must equal the sum of `columnWidths`
   203	- Cell `width` must match corresponding `columnWidth`
   204	- Cell `margins` are internal padding - they reduce content area, not add to cell width
   205	- For full-width tables: use content width (page width minus left and right margins)
   206	
   207	### Images

   211	new Paragraph({
   212	  children: [new ImageRun({
   213	    type: "png", // Required: png, jpg, jpeg, gif, bmp, svg
   214	    data: fs.readFileSync("image.png"),
   215	    transformation: { width: 200, height: 150 },
   216	    altText: { title: "Title", description: "Desc", name: "Name" } // All three required
   217	  })]

   225	new Paragraph({ children: [new PageBreak()] })
   226	
   227	// Or use pageBreakBefore
   228	new Paragraph({ pageBreakBefore: true, children: [new TextRun("New page")] })
   229	```

   231	### Table of Contents
   232	
   233	```javascript

   235	new TableOfContents("Table of Contents", { hyperlink: true, headingStyleRange: "1-3" })

   238	### Headers/Footers

   242	  properties: {
   243	    page: { margin: { top: 1440, right: 1440, bottom: 1440, left: 1440 } } // 1440 = 1 inch
   244	  },

   256	
   257	### Critical Rules for docx-js
   258	
   259	- **Set page size explicitly** - docx-js defaults to A4; use US Letter (12240 x 15840 DXA) for US documents
   260	- **Never use `\n`** - use separate Paragraph elements
   261	- **Never use unicode bullets** - use `LevelFormat.BULLET` with numbering config
   262	- **PageBreak must be in Paragraph** - standalone creates invalid XML
   263	- **ImageRun requires `type`** - always specify png/jpg/etc
   264	- **Always set table `width`** - use `{ size: 100, type: WidthType.PERCENTAGE }` for full width
   265	- **Tables need dual widths** - `columnWidths` array AND cell `width`, both must match
   266	- **Table width = sum of columnWidths** - for DXA, ensure they add up exactly
   267	- **Always add cell margins** - use `margins: { top: 80, bottom: 80, left: 120, right: 120 }` for readable padding
   268	- **Use `ShadingType.CLEAR`** - never SOLID for table shading
   269	- **TOC requires HeadingLevel only** - no custom styles on heading paragraphs
   270	- **Override built-in styles** - use exact IDs: "Heading1", "Heading2", etc.
   271	- **Include `outlineLevel`** - required for TOC (0 for H1, 1 for H2, etc.)

   275	## Editing Existing Documents
   276	
   277	**Follow all 3 steps in order.**
   278	
   279	### Step 1: Unpack
   280	```bash
   281	python scripts/office/unpack.py document.docx unpacked/
   282	```
   283	Extracts XML, pretty-prints, merges adjacent runs, and converts smart quotes to XML entities (`“` etc.) so they survive editing. Use `--merge-runs false` to skip run merging.
   284	
   285	### Step 2: Edit XML
   286	
   287	Edit files in `unpacked/word/`. See XML Reference below for patterns.
   288	
   289	**Use "Claude" as the author** for tracked changes and comments, unless the user explicitly requests use of a different name.
   290

   293	**CRITICAL: Use smart quotes for new content.** When adding text with apostrophes or quotes, use XML entities to produce smart quotes:
   294	```xml
   295	<!-- Use these entities for professional typography -->

   297	```
   298	| Entity | Character |
   299	|--------|-----------|
   300	| `‘` | ‘ (left single) |
   301	| `’` | ’ (right single / apostrophe) |
   302	| `“` | “ (left double) |
   303	| `”` | ” (right double) |
   304	
   305	**Adding comments:** Use `comment.py` to handle boilerplate across multiple XML files (text must be pre-escaped XML):
   306	```bash
   307	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 0 "Comment text with & and ’"
   308	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 1 "Reply text" --parent 0  # reply to comment 0
   309	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 0 "Text" --author "Custom Author"  # custom author name
   310	```
   311	Then add markers to document.xml (see Comments in XML Reference).
   312	
   313	### Step 3: Pack
   314	```bash
   315	python scripts/office/pack.py unpacked/ output.docx --original document.docx
   316	```
   317	Validates with auto-repair, condenses XML, and creates DOCX. Use `--validate false` to skip.
   318	
   319	**Auto-repair will fix:**
   320	- `durableId` >= 0x7FFFFFFF (regenerates valid ID)
   321	- Missing `xml:space="preserve"` on `<w:t>` with whitespace
   322	
   323	**Auto-repair won't fix:**
   324	- Malformed XML, invalid element nesting, missing relationships, schema violations
   325	
   326	### Common Pitfalls
   327	
   328	- **Replace entire `<w:r>` elements**: When adding tracked changes, replace the whole `<w:r>...</w:r>` block with `<w:del>...<w:ins>...` as siblings. Don't inject tracked change tags inside a run.
   329	- **Preserve `<w:rPr>` formatting**: Copy the original run's `<w:rPr>` block into your tracked change runs to maintain bold, font size, etc.

   332	
   333	## XML Reference
   334	
   335	### Schema Compliance
   336	
   337	- **Element order in `<w:pPr>`**: `<w:pStyle>`, `<w:numPr>`, `<w:spacing>`, `<w:ind>`, `<w:jc>`, `<w:rPr>` last
   338	- **Whitespace**: Add `xml:space="preserve"` to `<w:t>` with leading/trailing spaces
   339	- **RSIDs**: Must be 8-digit hex (e.g., `00AB1234`)
   340	
   341	### Tracked Changes
   342	
   343	**Insertion:**
   344	```xml
   345	<w:ins w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   346	  <w:r><w:t>inserted text</w:t></w:r>
   347	</w:ins>
   348	```
   349	
   350	**Deletion:**
   351	```xml
   352	<w:del w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   353	  <w:r><w:delText>deleted text</w:delText></w:r>
   354	</w:del>
   355	```
   356	
   357	**Inside `<w:del>`**: Use `<w:delText>` instead of `<w:t>`, and `<w:delInstrText>` instead of `<w:instrText>`.
   358	
   359	**Minimal edits** - only mark what changes:
   360	```xml
   361	<!-- Change "30 days" to "60 days" -->
   362	<w:r><w:t>The term is </w:t></w:r>
   363	<w:del w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="...">
   364	  <w:r><w:delText>30</w:delText></w:r>
   365	</w:del>
   366	<w:ins w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="...">
   367	  <w:r><w:t>60</w:t></w:r>
   368	</w:ins>
   369	<w:r><w:t> days.</w:t></w:r>
   370	```
   371	
   372	**Deleting entire paragraphs/list items** - when removing ALL content from a paragraph, also mark the paragraph mark as deleted so it merges with the next paragraph. Add `<w:del/>` inside `<w:pPr><w:rPr>`:
   373	```xml
   374	<w:p>
   375	  <w:pPr>
   376	    <w:numPr>...</w:numPr>  <!-- list numbering if present -->
   377	    <w:rPr>
   378	      <w:del w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"/>
   379	    </w:rPr>
   380	  </w:pPr>
   381	  <w:del w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   382	    <w:r><w:delText>Entire paragraph content being deleted...</w:delText></w:r>
   383	  </w:del>
   384	</w:p>
   385	```
   386	Without the `<w:del/>` in `<w:pPr><w:rPr>`, accepting changes leaves an empty paragraph/list item.
   387	
   388	**Rejecting another author's insertion** - nest deletion inside their insertion:
   389	```xml
   390	<w:ins w:author="Jane" w:id="5">
   391	  <w:del w:author="Claude" w:id="10">
   392	    <w:r><w:delText>their inserted text</w:delText></w:r>
   393	  </w:del>
   394	</w:ins>
   395	```
   396	
   397	**Restoring another author's deletion** - add insertion after (don't modify their deletion):
   398	```xml
   399	<w:del w:author="Jane" w:id="5">
   400	  <w:r><w:delText>deleted text</w:delText></w:r>
   401	</w:del>
   402	<w:ins w:author="Claude" w:id="10">
   403	  <w:r><w:t>deleted text</w:t></w:r>
   404	</w:ins>
   405	```

# **PARTNERSHIP & COLLABORATION FRAMEWORK PLAYBOOK**
## Strategic Alliances for Medspa Growth

---

## 📋 PLAYBOOK OVERVIEW

This comprehensive partnership playbook is designed to systematically build strategic local partnerships that drive client acquisition without paid advertising spend. By leveraging complementary businesses and creating mutual value, you'll establish a sustainable referral network that compounds over time.

**Expected Outcomes (90 Days):**
- 5-10 active partnership agreements signed
- 20-50 new client referrals from partners
- Zero-dollar customer acquisition partnerships
- Established local brand presence
- Recurring referral pipeline

---

## 🎯 SECTION 1: PARTNERSHIP FOUNDATION

### Understanding the Partnership Mindset

**The Core Principle:** Every partnership must create mutual value. You're not asking for favors—you're building strategic alliances where both businesses win.

**Why Partnerships Work:**
- Zero or low customer acquisition cost
- Access to pre-qualified, aligned audiences
- Enhanced local credibility through association
- Compound marketing reach
- Long-term sustainable growth

**Your Ideal Partner Profile:**
- Shares similar target demographic (age, income, values)
- Non-competing services (complementary, not competitive)
- Similar brand positioning (luxury, wellness-focused, professional)
- Established local presence (300+ clients/members)
- Open to collaboration

---

## 💼 SECTION 2: THE 5 CORE DEAL STRUCTURES

Every partnership can be built using one of these five foundational structures:

### **STRUCTURE 1: Reciprocal Referral**
**How It Works:** Both businesses refer clients to each other with no financial exchange

**Best For:** Businesses with similar audience and trust-based relationships

**Example Deal:**
- You refer clients needing fitness/nutrition to their gym
- They refer members interested in aesthetic enhancement to you
- Both promote to email lists quarterly
- Track with unique promo codes

**Success Metrics:**
- Minimum 5 referrals per quarter (each direction)
- Track conversion rates
- Quarterly review meetings

---

### **STRUCTURE 2: Service Exchange**
**How It Works:** Trade services at equal value (no money changes hands)

**Best For:** Service-based businesses with comparable pricing

**Example Deal:**
- You provide: $400/month in treatments for studio owner + 2 instructors
- They provide: Unlimited classes for 3 of your staff ($450 value)
- Both businesses get team benefits + exposure to each other's clients
- Both promote partnership on social media

**Success Metrics:**
- Services redeemed monthly
- Staff satisfaction scores
- New client inquiries from partnership

---

### **STRUCTURE 3: Commission/Kickback**
**How It Works:** Partner receives 10-20% commission for every booked client they refer

**Best For:** High-volume referral sources (salons, stylists, personal trainers)

**Example Deal:**
- Hair stylist refers clients for facial/injectable treatments
- Stylist earns 15% of treatment value as commission
- Paid monthly via Venmo/Zelle
- Track with unique promo code per stylist

**Financial Model:**
- Average treatment value: $300
- Commission paid: $45 (15%)
- Your net: $255
- Still profitable + builds pipeline

---

### **STRUCTURE 4: Client Incentive/Discount**
**How It Works:** Offer partner's clients exclusive discount; they promote you

**Best For:** Businesses with large email lists or membership bases

**Example Deal:**
- Boutique gym members receive "20% off first treatment + free consultation"
- Gym promotes via monthly email blast + in-studio signage
- Your clients receive free trial class at gym
- Track redemptions with custom promo code

**Promotion Assets Needed:**
- Partner provides: Email blast, social post, physical signage
- You provide: Branded flyers, digital graphics, promo code

---

### **STRUCTURE 5: Gift Package Inclusion**
**How It Works:** Partner includes your service voucher in their client gifts/welcome packages

**Best For:** Real estate agents, wedding planners, luxury service providers

**Example Deal:**
- Real estate agent includes $150 medspa gift certificate in closing gifts
- Agent pays wholesale: $75 per certificate (50% discount)
- New homebuyers redeem within 90 days
- 20% convert to regular clients

**Why Agents Love This:**
- They need closing gifts anyway ($50-200 typical spend)
- Your certificates feel luxurious and memorable
- Helps them stand out from other agents
- You get qualified, affluent leads

---

## 🏋️ SECTION 3: FITNESS & WELLNESS PARTNERSHIPS

### Target Partners:
- Barre studios (Pure Barre, local boutiques)
- Pilates studios (Club Pilates, independent)
- Yoga studios (CorePower, boutique studios)
- CrossFit boxes
- High-end gyms (Equinox, Lifetime Fitness)
- Personal training studios
- Wellness centers

### Why This Category Wins:
These clients are already investing $150-250/month in wellness. They value self-care, preventative health, and appearance. They're health-conscious, disciplined, and willing to invest in results—your exact demographic.

---

### PARTNERSHIP A: Barre/Pilates/Yoga Studios

#### **DEAL OPTION 1: Class-for-Service Exchange**

**Structure:**
- **You provide:** $200/month in services for studio owner + 2 instructors
  - Monthly facials ($75/each)
  - Or dermaplaning sessions
  - Or skin consultations + peels
- **They provide:** Unlimited monthly classes for 2-3 of your staff ($300-400 value)
- **Duration:** 6-month trial, review and renew
- **Promotion:** Both businesses promote to audiences (email, social, in-person)

**Value Exchange Breakdown:**
- **Studio gets:** Glowing skin for their visible brand ambassadors (instructors)
- **You get:** Healthy, energized staff + exposure to 200-500 wellness-minded women

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Identify 3-5 local studios to approach
2. Lead with benefit to them: "I'd love to help your instructors look and feel their best"
3. Propose trial period (3 months minimum)
4. Schedule monthly services at convenient times
5. Ask instructors to share experience organically (stories, mentions)
6. Track new client inquiries with "How did you hear about us?"

**Pitch Script:**
"Hi [Owner Name], I'm [Your Name] from [Your Medspa]. I've been following your studio and love what you're building. I have an idea that could benefit both of us: What if we created a wellness exchange where my team could provide complimentary monthly facials and treatments for you and your top instructors, and in exchange, a few of my staff members could join your classes? Your instructors are the face of your brand, and I'd love to help them glow even more. Plus, it would give our teams a chance to authentically experience what each of us offers. Would you be open to a quick call to discuss?"

---

#### **DEAL OPTION 2: Member Discount Program**

**Structure:**
- **Studio members receive:** 20% off first medspa service + free consultation
- **Your clients receive:** Free trial class at studio
- **Promotion Plan:**
  - Studio: Monthly email blast + in-studio signage + social media post
  - You: Email blast + social media + front desk handouts
- **Tracking:** Custom promo codes (e.g., PUREBARRE20, PILATESFLOW20)

**Marketing Assets You'll Need:**
- 8.5x11" posters for studio (you provide, branded beautifully)
- Social media graphics (square + story format)
- Email copy template
- QR code linking to booking page with discount auto-applied

**ROI Calculation:**
- Average studio: 250 members
- Email open rate: 25% = 62 people see offer
- Conversion rate: 5% = 3 new clients per month
- Average client value: $300 first visit
- Monthly new revenue: $900
- Annual value: $10,800
- **Cost to you:** Design time + 20% discount = minimal

---

#### **DEAL OPTION 3: Quarterly Wellness Event**

**Structure:**
- **Co-host "Wellness & Beauty Night" quarterly**
- **Studio provides:** Space, promotes to members, handles RSVPs
- **You provide:** Mini consultations, skin analysis, product demos, educational content
- **Split costs:** 50/50 for refreshments and marketing materials (typically $200-400 total)
- **Attendee perks:** Exclusive discounts from both businesses

**Event Format (2-hour evening):**
- 6:00-6:15pm: Check-in, refreshments, mingling
- 6:15-6:45pm: 30-minute class (yoga/barre) led by studio
- 6:45-7:45pm: Skin health workshop + mini-consultations rotating
- 7:45-8:00pm: Q&A, special offers revealed, booking incentives

**Event Promotion Timeline:**
- 4 weeks out: Save the date (social + email)
- 3 weeks out: Registration opens (limited to 20-30 attendees)
- 2 weeks out: Reminder + last spots available
- 1 week out: Final reminder + event details
- Day of: Stories, behind-the-scenes content
- Day after: Thank you post + recap

**Expected Outcomes:**
- 20-30 attendees
- 30-50% book consultation/first treatment
- 6-15 new clients
- Relationship deepened with studio
- Content for social media for next 2-3 months

---

### PARTNERSHIP B: Gyms & CrossFit Boxes

#### **DEAL OPTION 1: Recovery & Aesthetics Package**

**Structure:**
- **Create joint "Recovery + Glow" package**
- **Gym provides:** 1 month unlimited classes + 2 recovery sessions (massage, cryo, stretch)
- **You provide:** Signature facial + body contouring consultation + treatment
- **Package price:** $499 (normally $650-700 combined value)
- **Revenue split:** 50/50 ($250 each)
- **Sold by:** Both businesses (whoever sells it gets credit, revenue split after redemption)

**Positioning:**
"Work Hard, Recover Right, Look Amazing"
"The complete package for your fitness journey—build strength, recover faster, and enhance your results"

**Target Audience:**
- New year resolution crowd (Jan-Feb)
- Wedding season prep (Apr-Jun)
- Summer body push (May-Jul)
- Fitness competition prep

**Marketing Plan:**
- Co-branded package flyer at gym front desk
- Social media announcement (both accounts)
- Email to both lists
- Limited-time offer (creates urgency)
- Track sales by location

---

#### **DEAL OPTION 2: Referral Commission Model**

**Structure:**
- **Gym earns 15% commission** on every new client they refer who books
- **You provide exclusive member discount:** 20% off body contouring, CoolSculpting, EMSculpt, muscle toning
- **Gym promotes via:**
  - Email newsletter (monthly feature)
  - Front desk signage (provided by you)
  - Locker room posters (provided by you)
  - Trainer recommendations
- **Track with:** Custom promo code (FITGLOW15)

**Why This Works:**
- Gym wants additional revenue streams
- Your services complement their fitness goals perfectly
- Members are already body-conscious and investing in appearance
- Commission incentivizes ongoing promotion

**Positioning Angle:**
"You're doing the work—maximize your results with body contouring"
"Accelerate your transformation with science-backed aesthetic treatments"

**Commission Payment Process:**
1. Client mentions promo code at booking
2. You track in spreadsheet: Client name, service, date, revenue, commission owed
3. Monthly payout on 1st of month (Venmo/Zelle)

**Pro Tip:** Start with one motivated trainer as a pilot. If they earn $200-300 in the first month, other trainers will want in.

### PARTNERSHIP C: Nutrition Coaches & Health Practitioners

## ⚠️ SECTION 13: COMMON PARTNERSHIP MISTAKES TO AVOID

### Mistake #1: Not Setting Clear Expectations
**The Problem:** Vague agreements lead to disappointment

**The Fix:** 
- Put everything in writing
- Define specific commitments
- Set minimum referral expectations
- Clarify promotion requirements
- Establish review timeline

---

### Mistake #2: Choosing the Wrong Partners
**The Problem:** Partner has wrong audience or values

**The Fix:**
- Vet partner's reputation first
- Ensure audience overlap
- Check brand alignment
- Start with short trial period
- Have exit clause in agreement

---

### Mistake #3: Creating One-Sided Deals
**The Problem:** Partner doesn't see enough value

**The Fix:**
- Always think "what's in it for them?"
- Make value exchange equal or favor them slightly
- Ask what they need
- Be flexible
- Over-deliver on your commitments

---

### Mistake #4: Not Tracking Performance
**The Problem:** Don't know what's working

**The Fix:**
- Use promo codes for every partner
- Track in spreadsheet or CRM
- Review monthly
- Calculate actual ROI
- Kill underperforming partnerships

---

### Mistake #5: Set It and Forget It
**The Problem:** Partnership fizzles out from neglect

**The Fix:**
- Monthly check-ins with partner
- Regular social media mentions
- Quarterly review meetings
- Celebrate wins together
- Keep it top of mind

---

### Mistake #6: Making It Complicated
**The Problem:** Partnership is too confusing to explain or execute

**The Fix:**
- Keep agreements simple
- Make it easy for partner to participate
- Provide all materials they need
- Automate where possible
- Reduce friction

---

## 🎯 SECTION 14: ADVANCED PARTNERSHIP TACTICS

### Tactic 1: The Partnership Network Effect

**Strategy:** Don't just partner with individual businesses—create a network of partners who also partner with each other.

**How It Works:**
1. Recruit 5-10 complementary businesses
2. Everyone refers within the network
3. Create "preferred partner" list
4. Host quarterly networking events
5. Cross-promote each other systematically

**Example Network:**
- Your medspa
- Boutique gym
- Nutritionist
- Hair salon
- Boutique clothing store
- Wellness center
- Yoga studio

**Result:** Instead of 1:1 partnerships, you create 1:many leverage. Every partner promotes all other partners.

---

### Tactic 2: The Exclusive Territory Model

**Strategy:** Create exclusive partnerships within specific categories

**How It Works:**
- "I'm looking for ONE premier gym partner in the area"
- "I can only work with ONE hair salon to maintain quality"
- Creates urgency and perceived value
- Partner feels special, commits more

**When to Use:**
- High-value partnerships
- Competitive markets
- When you want deep commitment

---

### Tactic 3: The Co-Created Product

**Strategy:** Create entirely new offering together

**Examples:**
- "Fitness & Facial" package with gym
- "Glow & Go" event series with boutique
- "Bridal Beauty Blueprint" with wedding planner
- Custom membership tier with partners

**Why It Works:**
- Neither business could offer it alone
- Creates something unique in market
- Both have ownership stake
- Built-in cross-promotion

---

### Tactic 4: The Partnership Pyramid

**Strategy:** Tier your partnerships by strategic value

**Tier 1: Platinum Partners (2-3 partners)**
- Highest strategic value
- Exclusive arrangements
- Deep integration
- Monthly meetings
- Significant resources invested

**Tier 2: Gold Partners (5-8 partners)**
- Strong value
- Standard agreements
- Quarterly meetings
- Moderate resource investment

**Tier 3: Silver Partners (10-15 partners)**
- Opportunistic value
- Light-touch relationships
- Annual check-ins
- Minimal resource investment

**Why This Works:**
Focus your energy where it matters most. Not all partnerships deserve equal attention.

# **PARTNERSHIP & COLLABORATION FRAMEWORK PLAYBOOK**
## Strategic Alliances for Medspa Growth

---

## 📋 PLAYBOOK OVERVIEW

This comprehensive partnership playbook is designed to systematically build strategic local partnerships that drive client acquisition without paid advertising spend. By leveraging complementary businesses and creating mutual value, you'll establish a sustainable referral network that compounds over time.

**Expected Outcomes (90 Days):**
- 5-10 active partnership agreements signed
- 20-50 new client referrals from partners
- Zero-dollar customer acquisition partnerships
- Established local brand presence
- Recurring referral pipeline

---

## 🎯 SECTION 1: PARTNERSHIP FOUNDATION

### Understanding the Partnership Mindset

**The Core Principle:** Every partnership must create mutual value. You're not asking for favors—you're building strategic alliances where both businesses win.

**Why Partnerships Work:**
- Zero or low customer acquisition cost
- Access to pre-qualified, aligned audiences
- Enhanced local credibility through association
- Compound marketing reach
- Long-term sustainable growth

**Your Ideal Partner Profile:**
- Shares similar target demographic (age, income, values)
- Non-competing services (complementary, not competitive)
- Similar brand positioning (luxury, wellness-focused, professional)
- Established local presence (300+ clients/members)
- Open to collaboration

---

## 💼 SECTION 2: THE 5 CORE DEAL STRUCTURES

Every partnership can be built using one of these five foundational structures:

### **STRUCTURE 1: Reciprocal Referral**
**How It Works:** Both businesses refer clients to each other with no financial exchange

**Best For:** Businesses with similar audience and trust-based relationships

**Example Deal:**
- You refer clients needing fitness/nutrition to their gym
- They refer members interested in aesthetic enhancement to you
- Both promote to email lists quarterly
- Track with unique promo codes

**Success Metrics:**
- Minimum 5 referrals per quarter (each direction)
- Track conversion rates
- Quarterly review meetings

---

### **STRUCTURE 2: Service Exchange**
**How It Works:** Trade services at equal value (no money changes hands)

**Best For:** Service-based businesses with comparable pricing

**Example Deal:**
- You provide: $400/month in treatments for studio owner + 2 instructors
- They provide: Unlimited classes for 3 of your staff ($450 value)
- Both businesses get team benefits + exposure to each other's clients
- Both promote partnership on social media

**Success Metrics:**
- Services redeemed monthly
- Staff satisfaction scores
- New client inquiries from partnership

---

### **STRUCTURE 3: Commission/Kickback**
**How It Works:** Partner receives 10-20% commission for every booked client they refer

**Best For:** High-volume referral sources (salons, stylists, personal trainers)

**Example Deal:**
- Hair stylist refers clients for facial/injectable treatments
- Stylist earns 15% of treatment value as commission
- Paid monthly via Venmo/Zelle
- Track with unique promo code per stylist

**Financial Model:**
- Average treatment value: $300
- Commission paid: $45 (15%)
- Your net: $255
- Still profitable + builds pipeline

---

### **STRUCTURE 4: Client Incentive/Discount**
**How It Works:** Offer partner's clients exclusive discount; they promote you

**Best For:** Businesses with large email lists or membership bases

**Example Deal:**
- Boutique gym members receive "20% off first treatment + free consultation"
- Gym promotes via monthly email blast + in-studio signage
- Your clients receive free trial class at gym
- Track redemptions with custom promo code

**Promotion Assets Needed:**
- Partner provides: Email blast, social post, physical signage
- You provide: Branded flyers, digital graphics, promo code

---

### **STRUCTURE 5: Gift Package Inclusion**
**How It Works:** Partner includes your service voucher in their client gifts/welcome packages

**Best For:** Real estate agents, wedding planners, luxury service providers

**Example Deal:**
- Real estate agent includes $150 medspa gift certificate in closing gifts
- Agent pays wholesale: $75 per certificate (50% discount)
- New homebuyers redeem within 90 days
- 20% convert to regular clients

**Why Agents Love This:**
- They need closing gifts anyway ($50-200 typical spend)
- Your certificates feel luxurious and memorable
- Helps them stand out from other agents
- You get qualified, affluent leads

---

## 🏋️ SECTION 3: FITNESS & WELLNESS PARTNERSHIPS

### Target Partners:
- Barre studios (Pure Barre, local boutiques)
- Pilates studios (Club Pilates, independent)
- Yoga studios (CorePower, boutique studios)
- CrossFit boxes
- High-end gyms (Equinox, Lifetime Fitness)
- Personal training studios
- Wellness centers

### Why This Category Wins:
These clients are already investing $150-250/month in wellness. They value self-care, preventative health, and appearance. They're health-conscious, disciplined, and willing to invest in results—your exact demographic.

---

### PARTNERSHIP A: Barre/Pilates/Yoga Studios

#### **DEAL OPTION 1: Class-for-Service Exchange**

**Structure:**
- **You provide:** $200/month in services for studio owner + 2 instructors
  - Monthly facials ($75/each)
  - Or dermaplaning sessions
  - Or skin consultations + peels
- **They provide:** Unlimited monthly classes for 2-3 of your staff ($300-400 value)
- **Duration:** 6-month trial, review and renew
- **Promotion:** Both businesses promote to audiences (email, social, in-person)

**Value Exchange Breakdown:**
- **Studio gets:** Glowing skin for their visible brand ambassadors (instructors)
- **You get:** Healthy, energized staff + exposure to 200-500 wellness-minded women

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Identify 3-5 local studios to approach
2. Lead with benefit to them: "I'd love to help your instructors look and feel their best"
3. Propose trial period (3 months minimum)
4. Schedule monthly services at convenient times
5. Ask instructors to share experience organically (stories, mentions)
6. Track new client inquiries with "How did you hear about us?"

**Pitch Script:**
"Hi [Owner Name], I'm [Your Name] from [Your Medspa]. I've been following your studio and love what you're building. I have an idea that could benefit both of us: What if we created a wellness exchange where my team could provide complimentary monthly facials and treatments for you and your top instructors, and in exchange, a few of my staff members could join your classes? Your instructors are the face of your brand, and I'd love to help them glow even more. Plus, it would give our teams a chance to authentically experience what each of us offers. Would you be open to a quick call to discuss?"

---

#### **DEAL OPTION 2: Member Discount Program**

**Structure:**
- **Studio members receive:** 20% off first medspa service + free consultation
- **Your clients receive:** Free trial class at studio
- **Promotion Plan:**
  - Studio: Monthly email blast + in-studio signage + social media post
  - You: Email blast + social media + front desk handouts
- **Tracking:** Custom promo codes (e.g., PUREBARRE20, PILATESFLOW20)

**Marketing Assets You'll Need:**
- 8.5x11" posters for studio (you provide, branded beautifully)
- Social media graphics (square + story format)
- Email copy template
- QR code linking to booking page with discount auto-applied

**ROI Calculation:**
- Average studio: 250 members
- Email open rate: 25% = 62 people see offer
- Conversion rate: 5% = 3 new clients per month
- Average client value: $300 first visit
- Monthly new revenue: $900
- Annual value: $10,800
- **Cost to you:** Design time + 20% discount = minimal

---

#### **DEAL OPTION 3: Quarterly Wellness Event**

**Structure:**
- **Co-host "Wellness & Beauty Night" quarterly**
- **Studio provides:** Space, promotes to members, handles RSVPs
- **You provide:** Mini consultations, skin analysis, product demos, educational content
- **Split costs:** 50/50 for refreshments and marketing materials (typically $200-400 total)
- **Attendee perks:** Exclusive discounts from both businesses

**Event Format (2-hour evening):**
- 6:00-6:15pm: Check-in, refreshments, mingling
- 6:15-6:45pm: 30-minute class (yoga/barre) led by studio
- 6:45-7:45pm: Skin health workshop + mini-consultations rotating
- 7:45-8:00pm: Q&A, special offers revealed, booking incentives

**Event Promotion Timeline:**
- 4 weeks out: Save the date (social + email)
- 3 weeks out: Registration opens (limited to 20-30 attendees)
- 2 weeks out: Reminder + last spots available
- 1 week out: Final reminder + event details
- Day of: Stories, behind-the-scenes content
- Day after: Thank you post + recap

**Expected Outcomes:**
- 20-30 attendees
- 30-50% book consultation/first treatment
- 6-15 new clients
- Relationship deepened with studio
- Content for social media for next 2-3 months

---

### PARTNERSHIP B: Gyms & CrossFit Boxes

#### **DEAL OPTION 1: Recovery & Aesthetics Package**

**Structure:**
- **Create joint "Recovery + Glow" package**
- **Gym provides:** 1 month unlimited classes + 2 recovery sessions (massage, cryo, stretch)
- **You provide:** Signature facial + body contouring consultation + treatment
- **Package price:** $499 (normally $650-700 combined value)
- **Revenue split:** 50/50 ($250 each)
- **Sold by:** Both businesses (whoever sells it gets credit, revenue split after redemption)

**Positioning:**
"Work Hard, Recover Right, Look Amazing"
"The complete package for your fitness journey—build strength, recover faster, and enhance your results"

**Target Audience:**
- New year resolution crowd (Jan-Feb)
- Wedding season prep (Apr-Jun)
- Summer body push (May-Jul)
- Fitness competition prep

**Marketing Plan:**
- Co-branded package flyer at gym front desk
- Social media announcement (both accounts)
- Email to both lists
- Limited-time offer (creates urgency)
- Track sales by location

---

#### **DEAL OPTION 2: Referral Commission Model**

**Structure:**
- **Gym earns 15% commission** on every new client they refer who books
- **You provide exclusive member discount:** 20% off body contouring, CoolSculpting, EMSculpt, muscle toning
- **Gym promotes via:**
  - Email newsletter (monthly feature)
  - Front desk signage (provided by you)
  - Locker room posters (provided by you)
  - Trainer recommendations
- **Track with:** Custom promo code (FITGLOW15)

**Why This Works:**
- Gym wants additional revenue streams
- Your services complement their fitness goals perfectly
- Members are already body-conscious and investing in appearance
- Commission incentivizes ongoing promotion

**Positioning Angle:**
"You're doing the work—maximize your results with body contouring"
"Accelerate your transformation with science-backed aesthetic treatments"

**Commission Payment Process:**
1. Client mentions promo code at booking
2. You track in spreadsheet: Client name, service, date, revenue, commission owed
3. Monthly payout on 1st of month (Venmo/Zelle)
4. Provide summary report to gym showing referrals + earnings

**Pro Tip:** Start with one motivated trainer as a pilot. If they earn $200-300 in the first month, other trainers will want in.

---

### PARTNERSHIP C: Nutrition Coaches & Health Practitioners

#### **DEAL OPTION 1: Holistic Wellness Alliance**

**Structure:**
- **Cross-referral partnership** (no commission, pure value alignment)
- **You refer:** Clients needing nutrition guidance, meal planning, weight loss support
- **They refer:** Clients wanting to enhance appearance while improving health
- **Joint offerings:** Package nutrition coaching + aesthetic treatments for comprehensive transformation

**Target Partners:**
- Registered dietitians
- Health coaches
- Functional medicine practitioners
- GLP-1/weight loss clinics

**Why This Partnership Matters:**
Many medspa clients are on weight loss journeys. Many nutrition clients want to look as good as they feel. This creates a natural, holistic referral loop.

**Implementation:**
- Monthly coffee meetings to discuss client success stories
- Co-create "Total Transformation" package
- Guest post on each other's social media
- Share educational content

---

## 🛍️ SECTION 4: RETAIL & BOUTIQUE PARTNERSHIPS

### Target Partners:
- Women's clothing boutiques
- Luxury consignment shops
- Jewelry stores
- Home decor boutiques
- Spa/bath product retailers
- High-end gift shops

### Why This Category Wins:
Boutique shoppers are image-conscious, have disposable income, appreciate luxury experiences, and trust curated recommendations from their favorite shops.

---

### PARTNERSHIP A: Local Boutiques & Fashion Retailers

#### **DEAL OPTION 1: VIP Shopping Event**

**Structure:**
- **Co-host "Glow & Shop" evening quarterly**
- **Boutique provides:**
  - Space (after hours)
  - Light refreshments (wine, sparkling water, light apps)
  - 20% discount for all attendees
  - Promotes to email list + top customers
- **You provide:**
  - 10-15 minute mini facials (rotating stations)
  - Skin consultations
  - Product samples
  - Exclusive event-only treatment discount (25% off if booked that night)
- **Attendance:** Invite-only, 25-40 attendees

**Event Flow:**
- 6:00-7:00pm: Shop + skin consultations + mini treatments
- 7:00-7:15pm: Brief presentation on seasonal skincare
- 7:15-8:00pm: Continue shopping + consultations
- 8:00pm: Raffle drawing (gift basket from both businesses)

**Expected Outcomes:**
- 25-40 attendees
- 40-60% book full treatment within 30 days
- 10-20 new clients
- Deepened relationship with boutique owner
- Social content for 2-3 months

**Event Promotion:**
- 3 weeks out: Invitation sent (email + text to VIPs)
- 2 weeks out: Social media tease (both accounts)
- 1 week out: Reminder to RSVPs
- Day before: Final reminder + logistics
- Day of: Instagram Stories throughout
- Week after: Thank you post + recap

---

#### **DEAL OPTION 2: Reciprocal Gift with Purchase**

**Structure:**
- **Boutique includes:** Your $50 medspa gift card with purchases over $200
- **You include:** Their $25 boutique gift card with treatment packages over $300
- **Duration:** 3-6 month campaign
- **Both businesses:**
  - Display partner signage prominently
  - Mention in email newsletters
  - Social media posts
  - Train staff to mention the offer

**Gift Card Design:**
Make it beautiful—this represents your brand. Consider:
- Premium cardstock
- Elegant design matching your aesthetic
- Clear expiration (90-120 days is ideal)
- Booking instructions
- May not be combined with other offers (optional)

**ROI for Boutique:**
- Cost per card: $25 (your wholesale cost)

## ⚠️ SECTION 13: COMMON PARTNERSHIP MISTAKES TO AVOID

### Mistake #1: Not Setting Clear Expectations
**The Problem:** Vague agreements lead to disappointment

**The Fix:** 
- Put everything in writing
- Define specific commitments
- Set minimum referral expectations
- Clarify promotion requirements
- Establish review timeline

---

### Mistake #2: Choosing the Wrong Partners
**The Problem:** Partner has wrong audience or values

**The Fix:**
- Vet partner's reputation first
- Ensure audience overlap
- Check brand alignment
- Start with short trial period
- Have exit clause in agreement

---

### Mistake #3: Creating One-Sided Deals
**The Problem:** Partner doesn't see enough value

**The Fix:**
- Always think "what's in it for them?"
- Make value exchange equal or favor them slightly
- Ask what they need
- Be flexible
- Over-deliver on your commitments

---

### Mistake #4: Not Tracking Performance
**The Problem:** Don't know what's working

**The Fix:**
- Use promo codes for every partner
- Track in spreadsheet or CRM
- Review monthly
- Calculate actual ROI
- Kill underperforming partnerships

---

### Mistake #5: Set It and Forget It
**The Problem:** Partnership fizzles out from neglect

**The Fix:**
- Monthly check-ins with partner
- Regular social media mentions
- Quarterly review meetings
- Celebrate wins together
- Keep it top of mind

---

### Mistake #6: Making It Complicated

- Automate where possible
- Reduce friction

## 🎯 SECTION 14: ADVANCED PARTNERSHIP TACTICS

### Tactic 1: The Partnership Network Effect

**Strategy:** Don't just partner with individual businesses—create a network of partners who also partner with each other.

**How It Works:**
1. Recruit 5-10 complementary businesses
2. Everyone refers within the network
3. Create "preferred partner" list
4. Host quarterly networking events
5. Cross-promote each other systematically

**Example Network:**
- Your medspa
- Boutique gym
- Nutritionist
- Hair salon
- Boutique clothing store
- Wellness center
- Yoga studio

**Result:** Instead of 1:1 partnerships, you create 1:many leverage. Every partner promotes all other partners.

---

### Tactic 2: The Exclusive Territory Model

**Strategy:** Create exclusive partnerships within specific categories

**How It Works:**
- "I'm looking for ONE premier gym partner in the area"
- "I can only work with ONE hair salon to maintain quality"
- Creates urgency and perceived value
- Partner feels special, commits more

**When to Use:**
- High-value partnerships
- Competitive markets
- When you want deep commitment

---

**Strategy:** Create entirely new offering together

**Examples:**
- "Fitness & Facial" package with gym
- "Glow & Go" event series with boutique

- Custom membership tier with partners

**Why It Works:**
- Neither business could offer it alone
- Creates something unique in market
- Both have ownership stake
- Built-in cross-promotion

---

### Tactic 4: The Partnership Pyramid

**Strategy:** Tier your partnerships by strategic value

**Tier 1: Platinum Partners (2-3 partners)**
- Highest strategic value
- Exclusive arrangements

**Tier 2: Gold Partners (5-8 partners)**

- Opportunistic value
- Light-touch relationships
- Annual check-ins
- Minimal resource investment

**Why This Works:**
Focus your energy where it matters most. Not all partnerships deserve equal attention.

## 📋 PLAYBOOK OVERVIEW

This comprehensive partnership playbook is designed to systematically build strategic local partnerships that drive client acquisition without paid advertising spend. By leveraging complementary businesses and creating mutual value, you'll establish a sustainable referral network that compounds over time.

**Expected Outcomes (90 Days):**
- 5-10 active partnership agreements signed

- Zero-dollar customer acquisition partnerships
- Established local brand presence
- Recurring referral pipeline

## 🎯 SECTION 1: PARTNERSHIP FOUNDATION

### Understanding the Partnership Mindset

**The Core Principle:** Every partnership must create mutual value. You're not asking for favors—you're building strategic alliances where both businesses win.

**Why Partnerships Work:**
- Zero or low customer acquisition cost
- Access to pre-qualified, aligned audiences
- Enhanced local credibility through association
- Compound marketing reach
- Long-term sustainable growth

**Your Ideal Partner Profile:**
- Shares similar target demographic (age, income, values)
- Non-competing services (complementary, not competitive)
- Similar brand positioning (luxury, wellness-focused, professional)
- Established local presence (300+ clients/members)
- Open to collaboration

## 💼 SECTION 2: THE 5 CORE DEAL STRUCTURES

Every partnership can be built using one of these five foundational structures:

### **STRUCTURE 1: Reciprocal Referral**
**How It Works:** Both businesses refer clients to each other with no financial exchange

**Best For:** Businesses with similar audience and trust-based relationships

**Example Deal:**
- You refer clients needing fitness/nutrition to their gym
- They refer members interested in aesthetic enhancement to you
- Both promote to email lists quarterly
- Track with unique promo codes

**Success Metrics:**
- Minimum 5 referrals per quarter (each direction)
- Track conversion rates
- Quarterly review meetings

---

### **STRUCTURE 2: Service Exchange**
**How It Works:** Trade services at equal value (no money changes hands)

**Best For:** Service-based businesses with comparable pricing

**Example Deal:**
- You provide: $400/month in treatments for studio owner + 2 instructors
- They provide: Unlimited classes for 3 of your staff ($450 value)
- Both businesses get team benefits + exposure to each other's clients
- Both promote partnership on social media

**Success Metrics:**
- Services redeemed monthly
- Staff satisfaction scores
- New client inquiries from partnership

---

### **STRUCTURE 3: Commission/Kickback**
**How It Works:** Partner receives 10-20% commission for every booked client they refer

**Best For:** High-volume referral sources (salons, stylists, personal trainers)

**Example Deal:**
- Hair stylist refers clients for facial/injectable treatments
- Stylist earns 15% of treatment value as commission
- Paid monthly via Venmo/Zelle
- Track with unique promo code per stylist

**Financial Model:**
- Average treatment value: $300
- Commission paid: $45 (15%)
- Your net: $255
- Still profitable + builds pipeline

---

### **STRUCTURE 4: Client Incentive/Discount**
**How It Works:** Offer partner's clients exclusive discount; they promote you

**Best For:** Businesses with large email lists or membership bases

**Example Deal:**
- Boutique gym members receive "20% off first treatment + free consultation"
- Gym promotes via monthly email blast + in-studio signage
- Your clients receive free trial class at gym
- Track redemptions with custom promo code

**Promotion Assets Needed:**
- Partner provides: Email blast, social post, physical signage
- You provide: Branded flyers, digital graphics, promo code

---

### **STRUCTURE 5: Gift Package Inclusion**
**How It Works:** Partner includes your service voucher in their client gifts/welcome packages

**Best For:** Real estate agents, wedding planners, luxury service providers

**Example Deal:**
- Real estate agent includes $150 medspa gift certificate in closing gifts
- Agent pays wholesale: $75 per certificate (50% discount)
- New homebuyers redeem within 90 days
- 20% convert to regular clients

**Why Agents Love This:**
- They need closing gifts anyway ($50-200 typical spend)
- Your certificates feel luxurious and memorable
- Helps them stand out from other agents
- You get qualified, affluent leads

---

### PARTNERSHIP A: Barre/Pilates/Yoga Studios

#### **DEAL OPTION 1: Class-for-Service Exchange**

**Structure:**
- **You provide:** $200/month in services for studio owner + 2 instructors
  - Monthly facials ($75/each)
  - Or dermaplaning sessions
  - Or skin consultations + peels
- **They provide:** Unlimited monthly classes for 2-3 of your staff ($300-400 value)
- **Duration:** 6-month trial, review and renew
- **Promotion:** Both businesses promote to audiences (email, social, in-person)

**Value Exchange Breakdown:**
- **Studio gets:** Glowing skin for their visible brand ambassadors (instructors)
- **You get:** Healthy, energized staff + exposure to 200-500 wellness-minded women

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Identify 3-5 local studios to approach
2. Lead with benefit to them: "I'd love to help your instructors look and feel their best"
3. Propose trial period (3 months minimum)
4. Schedule monthly services at convenient times
5. Ask instructors to share experience organically (stories, mentions)
6. Track new client inquiries with "How did you hear about us?"

**Pitch Script:**
"Hi [Owner Name], I'm [Your Name] from [Your Medspa]. I've been following your studio and love what you're building. I have an idea that could benefit both of us: What if we created a wellness exchange where my team could provide complimentary monthly facials and treatments for you and your top instructors, and in exchange, a few of my staff members could join your classes? Your instructors are the face of your brand, and I'd love to help them glow even more. Plus, it would give our teams a chance to authentically experience what each of us offers. Would you be open to a quick call to discuss?"

## ⚠️ SECTION 13: COMMON PARTNERSHIP MISTAKES TO AVOID

### Mistake #1: Not Setting Clear Expectations
**The Problem:** Vague agreements lead to disappointment

- Define specific commitments
- Set minimum referral expectations
- Clarify promotion requirements
- Establish review timeline

**The Problem:** Partner has wrong audience or values

**The Fix:**
- Vet partner's reputation first
- Ensure audience overlap
- Check brand alignment
- Start with short trial period
- Have exit clause in agreement

---

### Mistake #3: Creating One-Sided Deals
**The Problem:** Partner doesn't see enough value

**The Fix:**
- Always think "what's in it for them?"
- Make value exchange equal or favor them slightly
- Ask what they need
- Be flexible
- Over-deliver on your commitments

---

### Mistake #4: Not Tracking Performance
**The Problem:** Don't know what's working

**The Fix:**
- Use promo codes for every partner
- Track in spreadsheet or CRM
- Review monthly
- Calculate actual ROI
- Kill underperforming partnerships

**The Problem:** Partnership fizzles out from neglect

- Celebrate wins together
- Keep it top of mind

- Reduce friction

## 🎯 SECTION 14: ADVANCED PARTNERSHIP TACTICS

### Tactic 1: The Partnership Network Effect

**Strategy:** Don't just partner with individual businesses—create a network of partners who also partner with each other.

**How It Works:**
1. Recruit 5-10 complementary businesses
2. Everyone refers within the network
3. Create "preferred partner" list
4. Host quarterly networking events
5. Cross-promote each other systematically

**Example Network:**
- Your medspa
- Boutique gym
- Nutritionist
- Hair salon
- Boutique clothing store
- Wellness center
- Yoga studio

**Result:** Instead of 1:1 partnerships, you create 1:many leverage. Every partner promotes all other partners.

---

### Tactic 2: The Exclusive Territory Model

**Strategy:** Create exclusive partnerships within specific categories

**How It Works:**
- "I'm looking for ONE premier gym partner in the area"
- "I can only work with ONE hair salon to maintain quality"
- Creates urgency and perceived value
- Partner feels special, commits more

**When to Use:**
- High-value partnerships
- Competitive markets
- When you want deep commitment

---

### Tactic 3: The Co-Created Product

**Strategy:** Create entirely new offering together

**Examples:**
- "Fitness & Facial" package with gym
- "Glow & Go" event series with boutique
- "Bridal Beauty Blueprint" with wedding planner
- Custom membership tier with partners

**Why It Works:**
- Neither business could offer it alone
- Creates something unique in market
- Both have ownership stake
- Built-in cross-promotion

---

### Tactic 4: The Partnership Pyramid

**Strategy:** Tier your partnerships by strategic value

**Tier 1: Platinum Partners (2-3 partners)**
- Highest strategic value
- Exclusive arrangements
- Deep integration
- Monthly meetings
- Significant resources invested

**Tier 2: Gold Partners (5-8 partners)**
- Strong value
- Standard agreements
- Quarterly meetings
- Moderate resource investment

**Tier 3: Silver Partners (10-15 partners)**
- Opportunistic value
- Light-touch relationships
- Annual check-ins
- Minimal resource investment

**Why This Works:**
Focus your energy where it matters most. Not all partnerships deserve equal attention.

### Understanding the Partnership Mindset

**The Core Principle:** Every partnership must create mutual value. You're not asking for favors—you're building strategic alliances where both businesses win.

**Why Partnerships Work:**
- Zero or low customer acquisition cost
- Access to pre-qualified, aligned audiences
- Enhanced local credibility through association
- Compound marketing reach
- Long-term sustainable growth

**Your Ideal Partner Profile:**
- Shares similar target demographic (age, income, values)

## 💼 SECTION 2: THE 5 CORE DEAL STRUCTURES

Every partnership can be built using one of these five foundational structures:

### **STRUCTURE 1: Reciprocal Referral**
**How It Works:** Both businesses refer clients to each other with no financial exchange

**Best For:** Businesses with similar audience and trust-based relationships

**Example Deal:**
- You refer clients needing fitness/nutrition to their gym
- They refer members interested in aesthetic enhancement to you
- Both promote to email lists quarterly
- Track with unique promo codes

**Success Metrics:**
- Minimum 5 referrals per quarter (each direction)
- Track conversion rates
- Quarterly review meetings

---

### **STRUCTURE 2: Service Exchange**
**How It Works:** Trade services at equal value (no money changes hands)

**Best For:** Service-based businesses with comparable pricing

**Example Deal:**
- You provide: $400/month in treatments for studio owner + 2 instructors
- They provide: Unlimited classes for 3 of your staff ($450 value)
- Both businesses get team benefits + exposure to each other's clients
- Both promote partnership on social media

**Success Metrics:**
- Services redeemed monthly
- Staff satisfaction scores
- New client inquiries from partnership

---

### **STRUCTURE 3: Commission/Kickback**
**How It Works:** Partner receives 10-20% commission for every booked client they refer

**Best For:** High-volume referral sources (salons, stylists, personal trainers)

**Example Deal:**
- Hair stylist refers clients for facial/injectable treatments
- Stylist earns 15% of treatment value as commission
- Paid monthly via Venmo/Zelle
- Track with unique promo code per stylist

**Financial Model:**
- Average treatment value: $300
- Commission paid: $45 (15%)
- Your net: $255
- Still profitable + builds pipeline

---

### **STRUCTURE 4: Client Incentive/Discount**
**How It Works:** Offer partner's clients exclusive discount; they promote you

**Best For:** Businesses with large email lists or membership bases

**Example Deal:**
- Boutique gym members receive "20% off first treatment + free consultation"
- Gym promotes via monthly email blast + in-studio signage
- Your clients receive free trial class at gym
- Track redemptions with custom promo code

**Promotion Assets Needed:**
- Partner provides: Email blast, social post, physical signage
- You provide: Branded flyers, digital graphics, promo code

---

### **STRUCTURE 5: Gift Package Inclusion**
**How It Works:** Partner includes your service voucher in their client gifts/welcome packages

**Best For:** Real estate agents, wedding planners, luxury service providers

**Example Deal:**
- Real estate agent includes $150 medspa gift certificate in closing gifts
- Agent pays wholesale: $75 per certificate (50% discount)
- New homebuyers redeem within 90 days
- 20% convert to regular clients

**Why Agents Love This:**
- They need closing gifts anyway ($50-200 typical spend)
- Your certificates feel luxurious and memorable
- Helps them stand out from other agents
- You get qualified, affluent leads

---

## ⚠️ SECTION 13: COMMON PARTNERSHIP MISTAKES TO AVOID

### Mistake #1: Not Setting Clear Expectations
**The Problem:** Vague agreements lead to disappointment

**The Fix:** 
- Put everything in writing
- Define specific commitments
- Set minimum referral expectations
- Clarify promotion requirements
- Establish review timeline

---

### Mistake #2: Choosing the Wrong Partners
**The Problem:** Partner has wrong audience or values

**The Fix:**
- Vet partner's reputation first
- Ensure audience overlap
- Check brand alignment
- Start with short trial period
- Have exit clause in agreement

---

### Mistake #3: Creating One-Sided Deals
**The Problem:** Partner doesn't see enough value

**The Fix:**
- Always think "what's in it for them?"
- Make value exchange equal or favor them slightly
- Ask what they need
- Be flexible
- Over-deliver on your commitments

---

### Mistake #4: Not Tracking Performance
**The Problem:** Don't know what's working

**The Fix:**
- Use promo codes for every partner
- Track in spreadsheet or CRM
- Review monthly
- Calculate actual ROI
- Kill underperforming partnerships

---

### Mistake #5: Set It and Forget It
**The Problem:** Partnership fizzles out from neglect

**The Fix:**
- Monthly check-ins with partner
- Regular social media mentions
- Quarterly review meetings
- Celebrate wins together
- Keep it top of mind

---

### Mistake #6: Making It Complicated
**The Problem:** Partnership is too confusing to explain or execute

**The Fix:**
- Keep agreements simple
- Make it easy for partner to participate
- Provide all materials they need
- Automate where possible
- Reduce friction

## 🎯 SECTION 14: ADVANCED PARTNERSHIP TACTICS

### Tactic 1: The Partnership Network Effect

**Strategy:** Don't just partner with individual businesses—create a network of partners who also partner with each other.

**How It Works:**
1. Recruit 5-10 complementary businesses
2. Everyone refers within the network
3. Create "preferred partner" list
4. Host quarterly networking events
5. Cross-promote each other systematically

**Example Network:**
- Your medspa
- Boutique gym
- Nutritionist
- Hair salon
- Boutique clothing store
- Wellness center
- Yoga studio

**Result:** Instead of 1:1 partnerships, you create 1:many leverage. Every partner promotes all other partners.

---

### Tactic 2: The Exclusive Territory Model

**Strategy:** Create exclusive partnerships within specific categories

**How It Works:**
- "I'm looking for ONE premier gym partner in the area"
- "I can only work with ONE hair salon to maintain quality"
- Creates urgency and perceived value
- Partner feels special, commits more

**When to Use:**
- High-value partnerships
- Competitive markets
- When you want deep commitment

---

### Tactic 3: The Co-Created Product

**Strategy:** Create entirely new offering together

**Examples:**
- "Fitness & Facial" package with gym
- "Glow & Go" event series with boutique
- "Bridal Beauty Blueprint" with wedding planner
- Custom membership tier with partners

**Why It Works:**
- Neither business could offer it alone
- Creates something unique in market
- Both have ownership stake
- Built-in cross-promotion

---

### Tactic 4: The Partnership Pyramid

**Strategy:** Tier your partnerships by strategic value

**Tier 1: Platinum Partners (2-3 partners)**
- Highest strategic value
- Exclusive arrangements
- Deep integration
- Monthly meetings
- Significant resources invested

**Tier 2: Gold Partners (5-8 partners)**
- Strong value
- Standard agreements
- Quarterly meetings
- Moderate resource investment

**Tier 3: Silver Partners (10-15 partners)**
- Opportunistic value
- Light-touch relationships
- Annual check-ins
- Minimal resource investment

**Why This Works:**
Focus your energy where it matters most. Not all partnerships deserve equal attention.

## 🏆 CONCLUSION

### The Partnership Advantage

While your competitors are spending $50-150 per lead on paid ads, you're building a network of strategic partners who send qualified referrals for free.

**The Math:**
- 10 partnerships × 5 referrals/month = 50 referrals/month
- 30% conversion = 15 new clients/month
- Average client value = $300
- **Monthly revenue: $4,500**
- **Annual revenue: $54,000**
- **Customer acquisition cost: ~$0**

**But It's Not Just About Revenue:**
- Enhanced local reputation
- Community presence
- Sustainable growth
- Recession-resistant (people still refer in downturns)
- Compounding returns (partnerships get better over time)

### The Partnership Mindset

The most successful medspa owners don't see other businesses as competitors or vendors—they see them as potential partners in a shared ecosystem.

When you partner strategically:
- Your brand is associated with quality
- Your clients get better overall experiences
- Your community sees you as connected and trusted
- Your business becomes more valuable (multiple revenue streams)

3. **This quarter:** Sign 3-5 partnership agreements and launch
4. **This year:** Build a network of 15-20 thriving partnerships

Partnerships aren't a marketing tactic—they're a growth strategy.

Start with one. Perfect it. Then scale.

Your community is full of potential partners who serve your exact clients. You just have to ask.
